subject: DPA redline: runtime access scope & rollforward/rollback safety
messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@caspian.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA draft (runtime access)

Jordan — attaching our internal redline (v3). Two clauses of concern for our platform team: the proposed "runtime access" language that would allow you to access request-level KV/cache artifacts for debugging, and the rollback/rollforward clause that implies we need to preserve versions for 12 months with guaranteed ability to revert.

We understand the need to debug but our security/compliance review flags any clause that allows provider-side access to per-request runtime state without stronger controls. Can you confirm:
- What exact runtime artifacts you need (KV cache keys vs full request payloads)?
- Whether access is interactive (ssh/console) or via a recorded audit bundle?
- Whether redaction/obfuscation is possible?

If you can propose precise, minimal-scope language we can move faster. Attached: Caspian-DPA-redline-v3.docx

Thanks —
Maya
Senior Counsel, Caspian AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@caspian.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA draft (runtime access)

Thanks Maya — good questions. Looping in Laura (Product) and Dev (Infra) to get a technical proposal and a security-safe fallback. High level response:

- Typical ask from customers is the ability for Redwood support/ops to collect a time-boxed runtime snapshot to diagnose production issues (e.g., KV-cache state for a single failing request). We do not require full unredacted customer payloads; default practice is to collect metadata, last n tokens in the buffer, and hashed keys for KV entries.

- Access modes we support today: (1) recorded diagnostic bundle delivered to customer for mutual review, (2) ephemeral, auditable read-only access via a jumpbox with recorded session, (3) automated anonymized telemetry. We can map any DPA language to these modes.

- Rollback/rollforward: our serving runtime supports pinned model versions and we keep model artifacts for 90 days in standard agreements; 12 months retention for rollback is operationally heavy and will materially change storage/retention costs.

Ask to Product & Security: can you review the attached runtime-access-matrix.xlsx and propose redline-friendly wording that limits access to "time-boxed diagnostic snapshots" with defined retention and approval flow? Also propose a plausible retention window for rollback artifacts (90/180/365) and an explanation of operational impact.

Jordan
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: runtime-access-matrix.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@caspian.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA draft (runtime access)

+1 to Jordan's framing. Quick product notes after reviewing the matrix and the doc:

- Minimal-scope proposal (aim for language): "Provider may collect time-limited diagnostic snapshots (limited to execution metadata, hashed KV indices, and the last 128 tokens of non-sensitive output) strictly for debugging and support. Provider will not retain unredacted request payloads beyond the diagnostic retention window, and will provide access logs to the customer upon request."

- For rollback/rollforward: Recommend we offer two tiers in the contract:
  1) Standard: 90-day model artifact retention and revert capability (no additional fee).
  2) Extended: 365-day retention and revert capability (additional fee and SLA for storage/restore time).

- Implementation caveats (Dev): rollback to older model versions requires snapshotting KV-cache-compatible checkpoints or draining active traffic and re-priming caches; restore time can vary (1-6 hours) and has cost implications.

If this is acceptable to legal, we can insert specific bracketed language in the DPA and mark the extended retention as an optional addendum.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@caspian.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA draft (runtime access)

Maya / Jordan — quick technical confirmation and a small ops ask:

- What we call a "diagnostic snapshot" will include: request metadata (request_id, model_version, route, timestamp), hashed KV keys (salted SHA256), last 128 tokens of generated output (configurable), and a single-line reason/notes field from the operator. No unredacted raw customer input will be included unless explicitly requested and approved under an Incident Response process.

- Access controls: any interactive access must be performed via our audited support console with MFA, SSO assertions, and recorded session logs; we can provide the recordings as part of evidence.

- On retention & rollback: we can do Standard 90-day retention with immediate revert tested in staging. For 365-day extended retention, we need an add-on that covers storage and restore SLAs; estimate incremental cost ~0.08 USD/GB/month and restores can take 1-8 hours depending on warm/cold state.

Next steps proposed:
1) Laura to provide bracketed DPA language for the two-tier retention + diagnostic snapshot definition.
2) Jordan to share bracketed language back to Caspian Legal and confirm pricing for extended retention.
3) If Caspian agrees, legal teams can exchange final redlines and sign the DocuSign envelope.

I attached a tiny operational matrix for the options.

- Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: runtime-access-matrix.xlsx]
